Error messages SHALL be localised per the request’s Accept-Language header.

Error responses SHALL NOT leak internal details: stack traces, SQL, internal hostnames, or other tenants’ data. Interactive clients SHALL authenticate using short-lived access tokens (15 minutes) with refresh tokens (30 days, rotating on use).
Machine clients SHALL authenticate using OAuth 2.0 client credentials or scoped API keys.
Tokens SHALL carry: subject, tenant, scope set, and permitted branch set. Every request SHALL be authorised against both the permission and the scope.
Refresh token rotation SHALL detect reuse of a consumed refresh token and SHALL revoke the entire token family on detection.
API keys SHALL be displayed exactly once at creation, stored as a hash, and identifiable thereafter only by a non-secret prefix.
Every POST and PATCH SHALL accept an Idempotency-Key header, and it SHALL be mandatory on all financially significant endpoints.
The System SHALL store the key, the request fingerprint, and the response for at least 30 days.
A repeated key with an identical request fingerprint SHALL return the stored response with Idempotent-Replay: true.
A repeated key with a different request fingerprint SHALL return 409 Conflict, because this indicates a client defect rather than a retry.
The System SHALL record an immutable audit entry for every statechanging operation.

Each audit entry SHALL contain: Field Content id ULID tenant_id, branch_id Scope Field Content occurred_at, recorded_at Business and system time actor_id, actor_type User, system, device, or integration impersonated_by Set when a support user is acting as a tenant user action Canonical verb, e.g. order.discount.applied entity_type, entity_id Target before, after JSONB state snapshots (changed fiel
Audit entries SHALL be append-only. The application database role SHALL hold INSERT and SELECT grants on the audit table and SHALL NOT hold UPDATE or DELETE.
Audit entries SHALL be hash-chained: each entry’s hash covers its own content and the previous entry’s hash, per tenant. hash(n) = SHA-256( canonical_json(entry_n) || hash(n-1) )

A scheduled job SHALL verify chain integrity and SHALL raise a platformlevel security alert on any break. Rationale: Hash chaining does not prevent tampering by an actor with database access. It makes tampering detectable, which is what an auditor requires and what makes the log admissible as evidence in a dispute with an employee or a franchisee. A log that could have been silently edited proves

The following actions SHALL always generate audit entries: authentication success and failure, permission changes, role changes, price changes, recipe changes, discounts, comps, voids, refunds, cash variances, stock adjustments, count postings, waste records, purchase approvals, configuration changes, data exports, integration credential changes, and impersonation sessions.
Audit log access SHALL itself be audited.
The audit log SHALL be searchable and filterable by actor, entity, action, date range, branch, and correlation ID, and SHALL be exportable by users with audit.view plus report.export.
Audit entries SHALL be retained for the greater of 7 years or the statutory period of the branch’s jurisdiction.

Support staff access to tenant data SHALL require an explicit impersonation session with a recorded reason, a time limit, tenant-visible notification, and full audit capture of every action performed. Rationale: Vendor support access is a legitimate necessity and a genuine risk. Tenants must be able to see, after the fact, exactly what the vendor’s staff did in their account. Making this visible b
The System SHALL support an unlimited number of branches per brand and an unlimited number of brands per tenant, subject to plan limits.
Each branch SHALL hold its own: inventory, cash drawers, staff roster, operating hours, timezone, currency, tax configuration, and country pack assignment.
Branches in different countries SHALL operate under different country packs within one tenant, and consolidated reporting SHALL handle multi-currency correctly.

Consolidated multi-currency reports SHALL display both the original currency amounts and a converted total, with the conversion rate, rate source, and rate date shown explicitly. Rationale: A consolidated total that silently converts currencies at an unstated rate is a number nobody can reconcile or defend. Showing the rate and its date is what makes the figure usable in a board pack rather than m
The System SHALL support branch groups (regions, clusters, franchise territories) as a reporting and permission-scoping dimension.
The System SHALL support central menu and price management with perbranch override capability, and the System SHALL report which branches deviate from the brand standard.
The System SHALL support central recipe management with the same override-and-report pattern.

The System SHALL support a branch template: a new branch may be created by copying configuration (menu, stations, roles, settings, printers) from an existing branch. Rationale: A growing chain opens branches on a schedule. If opening branch 12 requires a week of manual configuration, the System becomes the bottleneck in the customer’s expansion — which is the worst possible position for a vendor w

The System SHALL provide a branch scorecard comparing branches on: net sales, transaction count, average order value, food cost %, labour cost %, prime cost %, waste %, variance value, void/discount rates, and average service time.
Comparison SHALL support normalisation by seat count, floor area, labour hours, and trading hours, so branches of different sizes are meaningfully comparable.
The System SHALL rank branches on any metric and SHALL indicate movement against the prior period.
The System SHALL highlight outliers, defined as branches deviating beyond a configurable number of standard deviations from the group mean on any tracked metric.
The System SHALL support like-for-like comparison, excluding branches open for less than a configurable maturity period from group averages.
The System SHALL support stock transfers between any two locations within a tenant, per
The System SHALL support transfer requests: a branch requests stock, the source location approves and dispatches.
The System SHALL suggest transfers where one location holds excess stock approaching expiry and another location shows a shortage of the same item.
The System SHALL model central kitchens as locations that consume input stock and produce output stock.
Production SHALL be driven by a production order specifying output item, target quantity, and target date.
A production order SHALL expand its recipe to compute required inputs, SHALL check availability, and SHALL flag shortages before production begins.
On completion, a production order SHALL record actual output quantity, consume input stock, produce output stock, and create an output batch with production date and expiry.
The System SHALL compute production yield variance: Yield Variance = Actual Output − (Theoretical Output from Actual Inputs) and SHALL report it by item, batch, date, and operator.
Production output cost SHALL be computed as the sum of consumed input costs plus configurable production overhead (labour, energy) per unit or per batch.
The System SHALL generate a production plan from branch demand forecasts and current branch stock, indicating what the central kitchen should produce for the next production cycle.
The System SHALL support distribution orders allocating produced quantities to branches, generating transfer movements and, where relevant, delivery manifests.
Where produced quantity is insufficient for all branch requests, the System SHALL support allocation rules: proportional, by priority ranking, or manual.
The System SHALL maintain full batch traceability from raw material receipt through production to the branch and to the customer order.
The System SHALL support internal transfer pricing between central kitchen and branch, enabling the central kitchen to be evaluated as a cost centre or a profit centre per tenant policy.
The System SHALL support franchise branches with restricted configuration authority: franchisees may operate but may not modify brand-controlled menu, recipes, or pricing.
The System SHALL compute franchise royalties as a configurable percentage of net sales, with reporting per franchisee per period.

The System SHALL provide franchisor visibility into franchisee operational compliance: menu deviation, price deviation, recipe deviation, and mandated-supplier usage. Chapter 18 — Customer & Loyalty | العمالء والوالء
The System SHALL maintain customer records with: name, phone (primary identifier), email, addresses, date of birth, preferred language, tags, and consent flags.
Phone number SHALL be the primary identifier, unique within a tenant, stored in E.164 format.

Customer creation from the POS SHALL require no more than phone number and name, completable in under 15 seconds. Rationale: Every additional required field reduces capture rate. A form demanding email, birthday, and address at the counter will be filled in with fake data or skipped entirely, and the resulting database is worse than none because it is trusted while being wrong.
The System SHALL maintain per-customer order history with full detail, retrievable from the POS.
The System SHALL compute per-customer: total spend, order count, average order value, first and last order dates, favourite items, preferred branch, preferred order type, and preferred day-part.
The System SHALL support multiple delivery addresses per customer with labels and delivery notes.
The System SHALL support customer blocking, preventing on-account sales or delivery to a flagged customer, with reason and audit record.
The System SHALL record explicit consent flags per communication channel and per purpose, with timestamp and source, and SHALL NOT send marketing communication absent recorded consent.

The System SHALL support customer data export and erasure requests, with erasure anonymising the customer record while retaining transactional and fiscal records as legally required. Rationale: Erasure cannot delete a sales transaction, because tax law requires its retention. The correct implementation replaces personally identifying fields with an anonymised token while preserving the financial r
The System SHALL support a points-based loyalty programme with configurable earn rate, redemption rate, expiry, and eligibility rules.
Points SHALL be earnable on net spend excluding tax and excluding already-discounted amounts, configurable per tenant.
Points SHALL be redeemable as a tender type at the POS, converting to a monetary discount at the configured rate.
The System SHALL support tiered loyalty with configurable thresholds, tier benefits, and tier review periods.
The System SHALL support a stamp-card model (“buy 9 coffees, get the 10th free”) as an alternative to points, configurable per item or item group.

Loyalty balances SHALL be maintained as an append-only transaction ledger, not as a mutable balance field. Rationale: A mutable balance combined with offline operation is a duplication vulnerability: a customer redeems the same points at two branches while both are offline. A ledger with server-side reconciliation on sync detects the double-spend, and the tenant’s configured policy determines whet
Offline loyalty accrual SHALL be permitted. Offline redemption SHALL be permitted up to a configurable per-transaction limit, with the risk of overdraw accepted and reported on sync.
The System SHALL provide the customer a loyalty balance view via a QR code on the receipt leading to a lightweight web page requiring no app installation.

The System SHALL support a promotion engine with conditions and effects. Conditions: date and time range, day of week, branch set, order type, channel, minimum order value, specific items or categories present, minimum quantity, customer tag or tier, first order, Nth order, and coupon code presence. Effects: percentage discount on order, percentage discount on qualifying items, fixed amount off, f
Promotions SHALL support usage limits: total redemptions, per-customer redemptions, and per-day redemptions.
Promotion evaluation SHALL be deterministic and identical offline and online, and is covered by the shared conformance suite.
The System SHALL support single-use and multi-use coupon codes, with bulk generation and per-code tracking.
The System SHALL report promotion performance: redemptions, incremental revenue, discount cost, margin impact, and redeeming customer profile.
Promotion stacking SHALL be governed by explicit configuration; the default SHALL be non-stackable with best-value selection.
The System SHALL compute RFM segmentation (Recency, Frequency, Monetary) and SHALL classify customers into actionable segments: champions, loyal, at-risk, hibernating, and new.
The System SHALL compute a churn indicator based on a customer’s own historical inter-purchase interval rather than a global threshold.
The System SHALL support exporting a segment for a marketing campaign, subject to consent flags. Chapter 19 — Reporting & Analytics | التقارير والتحليالت

On order completion, the System SHALL compute COGS by expanding each order line’s recipe to base ingredients, applying modifier recipe deltas, and valuing consumption at the item’s current cost per the configured costing method.
COGS SHALL be recorded on the order line as unit_cost_snapshot and SHALL NOT be recomputed retroactively when ingredient costs change.
The System SHALL report food cost percentage as: Food Cost % = COGS ÷ Net Sales × 100 where Net Sales = Gross Sales − Discounts − Refunds − Tax
Food cost percentage SHALL be reportable by item, category, branch, brand, day-part, order type, and date range.

The System SHALL compute contribution margin per item: Contribution Margin = Selling Price (ex-tax) − Direct Cost Contribution Margin % = Contribution Margin ÷ Selling Price (extax) × 100 Total Contribution = Contribution Margin × Units Sold

The System SHALL support inclusion of configurable non-recipe direct costs in the margin calculation: packaging (per order type), delivery commission (per channel), and disposables. Rationale: A burger with a 68% margin dine-in may have a 31% margin on a delivery aggregator once a 25% commission and packaging cost are applied. Restaurants routinely discover, too late, that their delivery channel i
The System SHALL compute channel profitability, showing revenue, COGS, commission, packaging, and net contribution per sales channel.
For a defined period and location, the System SHALL compute theoretical usage per stock item as the sum, across all sold items, of recipe-expanded ingredient quantities.

For the same period and location, the System SHALL compute actual usage as: Actual Usage = Opening Count + Purchases Received + Transfers In + Production Output − Transfers Out − Production Input − Closing Count

The System SHALL compute variance: Variance Quantity = Actual Usage − Theoretical Usage Variance Value = Variance Quantity × Current Unit Cost Variance Percentage = Variance Quantity ÷ Theoretical Usage × 100
Recorded waste SHALL be presented as a separate column so that the report distinguishes explained from unexplained variance: Unexplained Variance = Variance Quantity − Recorded Waste Quantity

The variance report SHALL be sortable by variance value descending, so that the largest financial losses appear first regardless of quantity. Rationale: Sorting by quantity variance surfaces flour and salt. Sorting by value surfaces the beef, the salmon, and the imported cheese. Only one of those orderings is useful. This sounds like a trivial UI decision; it determines whether the report changes

The System SHALL classify variance by likely cause using the following heuristics, presented as hypotheses rather than conclusions: Signature Likely Cause Consistent positive variance on one item across all shifts Recipe understates actual portion Variance concentrated in one shift pattern Portion control or theft in that shift High variance on high-value items only Theft Variance correlating with
The System SHALL compute variance at a per-shift granularity where opening and closing counts are available at that granularity, and SHALL fall back to the count period otherwise.
The System SHALL provide a variance trend view showing an item’s variance percentage over successive count periods.
The System SHALL report waste by value and quantity, grouped by item, reason, category, employee, station, day-part, shift, and branch.
The System SHALL compute waste as a percentage of both COGS and net sales.
The System SHALL compute a rolling baseline of expected waste per item and location, and SHALL flag deviations beyond a configurable number of standard deviations.

The System SHALL produce a “cost of waste” summary translating waste into the revenue required to offset it: Revenue Required to Offset = Waste Value ÷ (Average Contribution Margin %) Rationale: “You wasted 4,200 EGP this month” is abstract. “You wasted 4,200 EGP, which requires 6,800 EGP of extra sales to recover” is a sentence that changes behaviour. Framing matters, and the framing that works i
The System SHALL correlate waste by reason with operational factors (staffing level, order volume, new employee presence, equipment fault reports) to support rootcause analysis.
The System SHALL compute labour cost per shift from attendance records and configured hourly rates.

The System SHALL compute: Metric Formula Labour Cost % Labour Cost ÷ Net Sales × 100 Sales per Labour Hour Net Sales ÷ Hours Worked Covers per Labour Hour Orders (or Guests) ÷ Hours Worked Prime Cost COGS + Labour Cost Prime Cost % Prime Cost ÷ Net Sales × 100

The System SHALL display sales and labour on a common hourly axis so overand under-staffing by hour is visible. Rationale: Prime cost is the number experienced operators watch, because it captures the two variable costs that management actually controls. A prime cost above roughly 65% of net sales is a warning; above 70% the business generally cannot cover rent and overheads. Presenting it promine

The System SHALL produce a branch profitability summary: Gross Sales − Discounts − Refunds = Net Sales (excl. tax) − COGS = Gross Profit − Labour Cost = Contribution After Labour − Recorded Operating Expenses = Branch Operating Profit
The System SHALL support recording branch operating expenses (rent, utilities, maintenance) with category, recurrence, and allocation.
The System SHALL support branch ranking by any metric, with configurable normalisation (absolute, per seat, per square metre, per labour hour) so that branches of different sizes are comparable.
The System SHALL compute a break-even sales level per branch from fixed costs and average contribution margin, and SHALL show progress against it during the month.

The System SHALL monitor and flag the following patterns for review. Every flag is a prompt for human investigation, never an accusation. Pattern Signal Excessive voids Void count or value per employee exceeding peer baseline by >2σ Post-payment voids Any void occurring after payment initiation Refund concentration Refunds by one employee exceeding baseline Refunds to different tender Cash refund
Anomaly flags SHALL be visible only to users holding an explicit governance.view_anomalies permission.

The System SHALL present anomaly flags with the underlying evidence — the specific transactions, timestamps, and comparison baseline — so that a manager can evaluate them rather than accept them. Rationale: An unexplained accusation against an employee is worse than no detection at all. It produces false accusations, damages trust, and generates legal exposure. The System’s role is to direct atten
Baselines SHALL be computed per branch and per role, not globally, because normal void rates differ enormously between a fast-food counter and a fine-dining room.

High-volume, time-ordered tables SHALL be range-partitioned by time: Table Partition Key Interval Retention Online sales.orders business_day Monthly 24 months, then archived sales.order_line s business_day Monthly 24 months inventory.stock_ movements occurred_at Monthly 24 months governance.audit _entries occurred_at Monthly 12 months, then cold storage analytics.fact_s ales_line date_key Monthly
Partitions SHALL be created automatically at least 3 months in advance by a scheduled job, with alerting if creation fails.
Archived partitions SHALL be exported to object storage in a queryable columnar format and SHALL remain retrievable within the statutory retention window.
All schema changes SHALL be expressed as versioned, forward-only migrations checked into source control.
Migrations SHALL be backward compatible with the previously deployed application version, enabling zero-downtime deployment and rollback.

Breaking schema changes SHALL follow the expand–migrate–contract sequence: 1. Expand : add the new column/table, nullable, with no constraint. Deploy. 2. Backfill : populate in batches with throttling to avoid lock escalation and replication lag. 3. Dual write: application writes both old and new. Deploy. 4. Migrate : switch reads to the new. Deploy. Observe. 5. Contract : stop writing old; drop t
Migrations SHALL be tested against a production-sized dataset in staging with timing measured, and any migration exceeding a 5-second lock SHALL be rejected.
Adding a NOT NULL column to a large table SHALL use a nullable column plus a backfill plus a validated constraint, never a single blocking statement.
Backups SHALL be encrypted, and restore procedures SHALL be documented and rehearsed quarterly with recorded results.
The System SHALL support restoring a single tenant’s data without restoring the entire database, using logical export filtered by tenant_id. Chapter 26 — API Design | تصميم الواجهات البرمجية
The System SHALL model cash drawers as branch-level entities, with one open cash session per drawer at any time.
A cash session SHALL be bound to exactly one employee. Two employees SHALL NOT share an open session on the same drawer.

The System SHALL support shared-drawer mode where a branch policy permits multiple cashiers on one drawer, in which case accountability attaches to the shift rather than the individual, and this SHALL be visibly indicated as a reduced control environment.
Expected cash SHALL be computed as: Expected Cash = Opening Float + Cash Sales + Cash Tips (if placed in drawer) + Pay-ins − Cash Refunds − Pay-outs − Safe Drops ± Cash Rounding Adjustments
Cash variance SHALL be computed as Counted Cash − Expected Cash and SHALL be recorded on the session.
Variance beyond a configurable tolerance SHALL require a reason and approval by a user with cash.variance.approve, who SHALL NOT be the session owner.
Cash sessions SHALL be immutable once closed. Corrections SHALL be recorded as adjusting entries referencing the session.
The System SHALL record, per session and per day, totals by tender type: cash, each card scheme, each wallet, gift card, voucher, on-account, and aggregator-settled.
The System SHALL support reconciliation of card totals against the payment terminal’s batch settlement report, flagging differences.

The System SHALL support reconciliation of aggregator-settled orders against aggregator payout statements, computing expected payout net of commission and flagging discrepancies. Rationale: Aggregator payout reconciliation is a real and under-served pain. Aggregators deduct commissions, promotional contributions, cancellation adjustments, and fees in ways that are difficult to verify. Restaurants
The System SHALL support recording branch operating expenses with category, amount, payment method, supplier, date, attachment, and approval status.
Petty cash paid from the drawer SHALL be recorded as a pay-out linked to the expense record, so that the drawer reconciles.
Expenses above a configurable threshold SHALL require approval before posting.
The System SHALL support recurring expense templates for rent, utilities, and subscriptions.
The System SHALL support a business-day close operation per branch.
Day close SHALL be blocked while any cash session remains open, and SHALL list the blocking sessions.

Day close SHALL produce a Z report containing: gross sales, discounts, refunds, net sales, tax by rate, sales by category, sales by tender, sales by order type, transaction count, average order value, void and comp summary, cash reconciliation, and variance summary.
Z reports SHALL be sequentially numbered per branch, immutable, and retrievable for any historical date.
The System SHALL support a configurable business-day boundary per branch (e.g. 04:00), so that late-night trading is attributed to the correct operating day.
Day close SHALL be performable automatically at the configured boundary where the branch enables it, with any open sessions force-closed and flagged.
Day close SHALL trigger: fiscal document finalisation, inventory day-end snapshot, report pre-aggregation, and accounting export generation where configured.
Tax SHALL be computed by the country pack’s tax engine, never by hardcoded logic.
The System SHALL support tax-inclusive and tax-exclusive pricing, configurable per branch and per price list.
The System SHALL support multiple simultaneous tax components (e.g. VAT plus municipality fee plus service tax), each with its own rate, base, and rounding.
The System SHALL support tax classes per item (standard, reduced, zerorated, exempt) and SHALL support order-type-dependent rates where the jurisdiction differentiates dine-in from takeaway.

Tax SHALL be computed at line level and summed, not computed on the order total. Rationale: Computing tax on the order total rather than per line produces amounts that differ by one or two minor units from line-level computation, and tax authorities that validate submitted invoices will reject the discrepancy. Per-line computation with explicit summation is the only approach that reconciles with f
The rounding mode and rounding point SHALL be specified by the country pack and SHALL be applied consistently across POS, server, receipt, and fiscal submission.

The System SHALL maintain employee records containing: employee code, names (localised), national/residency identifier, contact details, emergency contact, date of birth, hire date, termination date, position, department, home branch, permitted branches, employment type, and status.
The System SHALL support employment types: full-time, part-time, casual, contractor, and trainee, with different rules for scheduling and overtime.
The System SHALL store compensation basis (hourly rate, monthly salary, or per-shift rate) with effective dating, and SHALL restrict visibility of compensation to holders of an explicit permission.

The System SHALL store document references with expiry dates (residency permit, work permit, health certificate, food-handling licence) and SHALL alert before expiry. Rationale: In GCC markets, expired residency or health certificates create immediate regulatory exposure for the employer. A restaurant inspected with a lapsed foodhandling certificate faces closure. Expiry alerting is a compliance f
Employees SHALL be assignable to multiple branches with a designated home branch, supporting the common practice of staff covering shifts across a group.
Employee records SHALL be deactivatable but SHALL NOT be deletable while historical transactions reference them.
The System SHALL support creating shift schedules by branch, week, position, and employee.
The System SHALL support shift templates and week-pattern copying to avoid rebuilding a schedule each week.

The System SHALL validate schedules against configurable rules and warn or block on violation: Rule Default Maximum consecutive working days 6 Minimum rest between shifts 11 hours Maximum shift length 12 hours Maximum weekly hours before overtime 48 Minimum staffing per position per hour Per branch configuration Employee availability and leave Must not conflict Required certification for position
The System SHALL project scheduled labour cost for the week and compare it against a configurable target percentage of forecast sales.
The System SHALL forecast required staffing per hour from historical sales patterns for the same weekday and season, and SHALL overlay this against the drafted schedule.
The System SHALL publish schedules to employees by mobile notification and SHALL record acknowledgement.
The System SHALL support shift swap requests between employees, subject to rule validation and manager approval.
The System SHALL support leave requests, approval workflow, and a leave balance per configured leave type.
The System SHALL support clock-in and clock-out via: POS terminal with PIN, mobile app with geofence validation, and biometric device integration where available.
The System SHALL record clock events with timestamp, method, terminal or device, and — where mobile — GPS coordinates.
The System SHALL detect and flag: late arrival beyond a grace period, early departure, missing clock-out, clock-in outside the geofence, and clock-in with no scheduled shift.
The System SHALL prevent a clock-in more than a configurable interval before the scheduled shift start, to prevent inflated paid hours.
Missing clock-outs SHALL be auto-closed at a configurable maximum shift length, flagged for manager correction, and SHALL NOT silently accrue hours.
Manual attendance corrections SHALL require a reason, SHALL be permission-gated, and SHALL create an audit entry retaining the original value.
The System SHALL support break tracking, distinguishing paid from unpaid breaks per configuration.

The System SHALL support photo capture at clock-in as a deterrent to buddy-punching, subject to explicit configuration and employee notice. Rationale: Buddy-punching (one employee clocking in for another) is the most common form of labour fraud. Geofencing addresses it for mobile clock-in; photo capture addresses it for terminal clock-in. Both are privacy-sensitive and must be optin per tenant wit

The System SHALL compute per-employee metrics: total sales, order count, average order value, items per order, upsell attachment rate, average service time, void count and value, discount count and value, and cash variance.
The System SHALL compute kitchen employee metrics from KDS data: items prepared, average preparation time by item, and remake count.
The System SHALL support ranking employees on any metric within a branch, position, and period.
The System SHALL compute worked hours, split into regular and overtime per the branch’s country pack overtime rules.
Overtime beyond a configurable threshold SHALL require pre-approval, and unapproved overtime SHALL be flagged in a separate report rather than silently included.

The System SHALL export payroll data in configurable formats (CSV with mappable columns, plus provider-specific templates) containing employee identifier, period, regular hours, overtime hours, absence, tips allocated, and deductions recorded.

The System SHALL NOT compute net pay, tax withholding, or statutory contributions. It exports inputs to payroll; it is not a payroll engine. Chapter 15 — Roles, Permissions & Access Control | األدوار والصالحيات

Every external system SHALL be accessed through an Anti-Corruption Layer that translates between the external model and the ROS domain model. External data structures SHALL NOT propagate into the domain.
All outbound integration calls SHALL be dispatched through the transactional outbox and SHALL be idempotent.
All inbound integration calls SHALL be authenticated, rate-limited, validated against a schema, and idempotent by an external reference key.
Integration failures SHALL be visible in an integration health dashboard showing per-connector status, last success, error rate, and queue depth.
Integration credentials SHALL be stored encrypted, SHALL be rotatable without downtime, and SHALL never appear in logs or error messages.
Each connector SHALL implement a circuit breaker: after a configured failure threshold, calls are suspended and queued, with periodic probing for recovery.

The System SHALL maintain a stock item master with the following attributes: Attribute Notes Code / SKU Unique per tenant Names (localised) Category Hierarchical: Food → Protein → Poultry Base unit of measure Immutable after first movement Purchase unit(s) With conversion factor to base unit Recipe unit Usually base unit Costing method FIFO, weighted average, or standard Batch tracked Boolean Expi

The base unit of measure SHALL be immutable once any stock movement exists for the item. Rationale: Changing the base unit after movements exist retroactively reinterprets every historical quantity. A change from kilograms to grams would multiply history by 1,000 and produce an inventory value in the millions. This must be structurally impossible, not merely discouraged.
The System SHALL support multiple purchase units per item with independent conversion factors, so an item may be bought in cases of 12 from one supplier and cases of 24 from another.
The System SHALL support mass↔volume conversion for an item where a density factor is configured, and SHALL reject such conversion where it is not.
The System SHALL support supplier-specific item codes and barcodes, so that a supplier’s invoice or delivery note can be matched automatically.
The System SHALL maintain current stock levels per (item, location) pair as a projection over the stock movement ledger.
Stock levels SHALL be reconcilable to the movement ledger at any point in time, and a scheduled job SHALL verify the reconciliation daily and alert on divergence.

The System SHALL support three costing methods, configurable per item: Method Computation Best For Weighted Average (existing_value + received_value) / (existing_qty + received_qty) recomputed on each receipt Most food items; simple and stable FIFO Consumption valued at the cost of the oldest remaining batch Items with volatile pricing; more accurate COGS Standard Cost Fixed cost per unit; purchas
Where an item is batch-tracked, FIFO valuation SHALL follow batch receipt order, and consumption SHALL record which batch was consumed.
The System SHALL permit negative stock levels, recording them and raising an alert, rather than blocking the transaction that causes them.
The System SHALL report total inventory value per location, per category, and per item, at any historical date, computed from the movement ledger.

For batch-tracked items, the System SHALL create a batch record on receipt or production, carrying: batch number, production date, expiry date, quantity, unit cost, supplier, and originating document.
The System SHALL default the expiry date from the item’s configured shelf life, allowing override at receipt.
The System SHALL support two consumption strategies, configurable per item: • FIFO — consume the oldest received batch first. • FEFO — consume the batch with the nearest expiry first.

FEFO SHALL be the default for items with expiry tracking enabled. Rationale: FIFO and FEFO diverge whenever a later delivery has an earlier expiry — which happens constantly in fresh produce and dairy, because suppliers rotate their own stock. Using FIFO on perishables systematically produces expired stock behind fresh stock. FEFO is the correct default for anything that spoils.
The System SHALL generate expiry alerts at configurable horizons per item category (default: 7, 3, and 1 days before expiry).

The System SHALL provide an expiry action worklist showing items approaching expiry, with quantity, value, and one-tap actions: mark wasted, transfer to another location, or create a markdown promotion.
The System SHALL support automatic write-off of expired batches at day close, configurable per item category, creating waste records with reason expired.

The System SHALL support batch traceability reporting: given a batch, list every order that consumed it (forward trace); given an order, list every batch consumed (backward trace). Rationale: This is a food-safety and legal requirement in an incident. If a supplier issues a recall on a specific lot of chicken, the operator must be able to answer, within minutes, which branches received it, how muc

Inter-location transfers SHALL be modelled as a two-step process — dispatch and receipt — creating paired movements, with quantity in transit visible between them.
The receiving location SHALL be able to record a received quantity differing from the dispatched quantity, creating a transfer discrepancy record requiring investigation and approval.
Transfers SHALL support a printed or digital transfer note with barcode/QR for scanning at receipt.
Transfers between locations with different costing bases SHALL transfer at the sending location’s cost, with the difference posted to a transfer variance account where configured.
Manual stock adjustments SHALL require a reason code, SHALL be permission-gated, and SHALL require approval above a configurable value threshold.
The System SHALL support stock count sessions covering: a full location, a category, a storage area, or an ad-hoc item list.
The System SHALL support two count modes: • Blind count — expected quantity is hidden during counting. • Open count — expected quantity is displayed.
Blind count SHALL be the default and SHALL be enforceable as mandatory by policy configuration.
The System SHALL support counting on a mobile device with barcode scanning, offline-capable, syncing on completion.

The System SHALL freeze the expected quantity at the moment a count session opens, and SHALL account for movements occurring during the count window so that the variance calculation is not corrupted by concurrent activity.
